turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Please sit, ma'am. Pressure is one twenty-eight over eighty-two, pulse seventy-six, saturation ninety-eight percent. Doctor will call you just now.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hello, I am Dr. Mehta. The waiting room is damp from the rain, sorry. Tell me, what is the problem?
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Lump. Left breast.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Umm, since when is this lump?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Diwali. Or after. Can't say.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any pain in it?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Uh, you found it how?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Shower.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any nipple discharge, blood or otherwise?
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Has it become bigger, or the skin over it changed?
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. That is not really a yes, I won't record it as such. Family side, who has had which illness, tell me properly.
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): Umm my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar. Mother had breast cancer at fifty-five.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Err, so mother had breast cancer at fifty-five. That we cannot ignore. You yourself are forty-three, correct?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any regular tablets?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Work, timings, food, exercise, alcohol, say it in one go.
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): I teach in a government school, eight to three, mostly rice and dal, evening walk in the colony, no alcohol.
[SEG0022] person_1 (NURSE): Ma'am, allergy to any drug or food?
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fever, weight loss, tiredness, any of these?
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): Breathing, waterworks, periods, all quiet?
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): Yes.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): I will examine now. Left breast, upper outer quadrant, there is a firm lump, about two centimetres, it moves, the skin is not pulled in.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Nipple is not retracted. Right side I am not feeling any lump. Armpit, no glands that I can feel.

[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Thinking it through, we should not sit on this. Painless lump, left side, mother had breast cancer. My working impression is this may be benign, something like a fibroadenoma, but I cannot rule out a cancer. We will not call it either way today.
[SEG0031] person_2 (DOCTOR): From my side the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning, full count and sugar. You come fasting, no breakfast.
[SEG0032] person_1 (NURSE): Thursday, eight in the morning, fasting only. The lift is out, use the stairs to the lab. I am writing your name in the register.

[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): If those are borderline we do the third test, the HbA1c. If the lump does not settle, a scan. Neither is booked today. I am not starting any tablet, no tamoxifin or painkiller.

[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): The urgent breast clinic referral I am putting through, they should see you this week. I will see you here in two weeks. Don't keep checking the lump with your hand. If you get sudden redness or fever, come sooner.
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): Okay.

spec.situation: Woman in her forties who found a painless lump in the left breast in the shower; no nipple discharge; mother had breast cancer at fifty-five; examination described; urgent clinic referral.

traps.happens: In ONE long answer the patient lists several relatives and their conditions ('my father had diabetes in his fifties, mother did not, another sister has pressure but no sugar'), and in another long answer their job, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol.
traps.label_rule: Every relative with a stated condition is a separate family_history entry (relative, condition). Relatives said NOT to have a condition are not family_history entries. Occupation, hours, diet, exercise and alcohol/tobacco each become social_history entries as said (no inventions). Nothing from the doctor's questions is a fact.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: vague_dates: the patient cannot date things ('since Diwali or after', 'last winter, or the one before'); no invented date; a date_uncertain item.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

bad.reason: Left breast lump and timing are supported; certainty 'certain' is wrong because patient was unsure of onset.
bad.text: Left breast lump (category=other, status=present, duration=since Diwali or after, temporality=current, body_site=left breast, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Doctor specifically did not record increase in lump size or skin change because the patient's reply ('I suppose') was equivocal, so this history is uncertain rather than positive.
Family history detail missing: mother did not have diabetes.
Planned investigations/referral were not booked today.
Doctor stated he was not starting any tablets, specifically no tamoxifen and no painkiller.
